args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- It's clean and loads instantly — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay. That's a genuinely pleasant first impression.
- The page tells the visitor right away what the site is (a personal site) and how to reach you, which is the most important thing to get right.

Where I'd love to see more:
- The site is currently just one line of text, so there's not much to explore. Even a short "About me" section (what you do, what you're interested in, where you're based) would give visitors a reason to come back.
- A few recent posts, a small photo gallery, or a list of your favorite links/projects would add personality and make the site feel lived-in.
- If you do share personal details, a short note about what you're happy to have public is a nice touch.

Overall it's a nice, tidy starting point — it just needs a bit more of your personality to really shine. Happy to share more specific thoughts if you'd like!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I just had a look at your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- The site is refreshingly simple and fast — no heavy theme, no distracting widgets, just your words.
- Leading with a personal touch (your love of hiking) gives readers an immediate sense of who you are and what the blog might be about.

Where I'd love to see more:
- Right now the blog is a single line, so there's no actual reading experience yet. A few full posts — even short ones — would give people a reason to subscribe and return.
- Since hiking is your thing, a "Best trails" or "Recent hikes" series would be a natural first series and a great hook for readers.
- Adding a small archive or tag list would make older posts easy to find once you have more of them.
- Photos from your hikes would add a lot of warmth and make the blog much more engaging.

Overall, the tone and simplicity are appealing — it feels like a blog that will stay pleasant to read. It just needs a few real posts to get going.

Best,
Emma Johnson
